```{r}
## Set ggplot theme
## Set ggplot theme
my_theme <- theme(line              = element_line(size=1.2),
                  rect              = element_rect(size=1.2),
                  text              = element_text(size=16,color="black"),
                  panel.background  = element_rect(fill="white",color="white"),
                  plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
                  strip.background  = element_blank(),
                  strip.text        = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
                  panel.grid.major  = element_blank(), 
                  panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
                  axis.text.x       = element_text(size=22,color="black"), #,angle=90),
                  axis.text.y       = element_text(size=22,color="black"),
                  axis.title.x      = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10, r = 0, b = 0, l = 0)),
                  axis.title.y      = element_text(margin = margin(t = 0, r = 10, b = 0, l = 0)),
                  axis.ticks.x      = element_line(color="black"),
                  axis.ticks.y      = element_line(color="black"),
                  # axis.line         = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.1),
                  panel.border      = element_rect(color = "black", fill=NA, size=1.2),
                  panel.spacing.x   = unit(1.0, "cm"),
                  panel.spacing.y   = unit(1.0, "cm"),
                  legend.key        = element_blank(), # removes background of legend bullets
                  legend.position   = "none"
                  ) 

# Create a sample data frame with "overlap" replaced by "interaction"
data <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("control", "heat", "heat", "heat", "control + heat", "control + heat", "control + heat", "control",
                "heat", "heat", "heat", "control + heat", "control + heat", "control + heat", "control", "heat", "heat", 
                "heat", "control + heat", "control + heat", "control + heat", "control", "heat", "heat", "heat", 
                "control + heat", "control + heat", "control + heat"),
  factor = c("ploidy", "ploidy", "heat", "interaction", "ploidy", "heat", "interaction", "ploidy", "ploidy", "heat", 
             "interaction", "ploidy", "heat", "interaction", "ploidy", "ploidy", "heat", "interaction", "ploidy", "heat", 
             "interaction", "ploidy", "ploidy", "heat", "interaction", "ploidy", "heat", "interaction"),
  variable = c("GO terms", "GO terms", "GO terms", "GO terms", "GO terms", "GO terms", "GO terms", 
               "Unique transcripts", "Unique transcripts", "Unique transcripts", "Unique transcripts", 
               "Unique transcripts", "Unique transcripts", "Unique transcripts", "Unique genes", 
               "Unique genes", "Unique genes", "Unique genes", "Unique genes", "Unique genes", "Unique genes", 
               "Gene products", "Gene products", "Gene products", "Gene products", "Gene products", 
               "Gene products", "Gene products"),
  BP = c(34086, 514086, 50696, 14503, 4379, 39688, 3332, 950, 17007, 412, 19517, 128, 93, 55, 29, 28, 8, 1, 1, 3, 1, 
         2736, 68452, 1236, 109458, 199, 1441, 165),
  CC = c(21772, 375681, 39736, 9588, 4145, 26084, 2337, 2705, 31297, 12821, 39913, 601, 727, 610, 21, 1313, 348, 331, 
         12, 17, 10, 3407, 259092, 20617, 39913, 1420, 1698, 1145),
  MF = c(14724, 235261, 23665, 5706, 2443, 15213, 1262, 1358, 22189, 1548, 13304, 178, 1841, 207, 52, 71, 27, 23, 6, 
         49, 4, 2288, 61978, 3861, 37810, 392, 5801, 318)
)

# Filter the data to only include rows for "control + heat" treatment
data_filtered <- data %>%
  filter(treatment == "control + heat")

# Ensure the variable column is ordered according to the specified order
data_filtered$variable <- factor(data_filtered$variable, levels = c("Unique transcripts", "GO terms", "Unique genes", "Gene products"))

# Reshape the filtered data to a long format for easier plotting with ggplot2
data_long <- data_filtered %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c("BP", "CC", "MF"), names_to = "Category", values_to = "Value")

# Ensure that the 'factor' column is ordered so that ploidy is first, heat second, and interaction third
data_long$factor <- factor(data_long$factor, levels = c("ploidy", "heat", "interaction"))

# Generate the bar plot for "control + heat" treatment only
p1 <- ggplot(data_long, aes(x = Category, y = Value, fill = factor)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(Value)), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
            vjust = -0.3, size = 3, fontface="bold") +  # Add text labels above each bar with thousand separators
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("ploidy" = "royalblue1", "heat" = "orangered1", "interaction" = "seagreen3")) +  # Custom colors
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +  # Set ncol = 2 for a 2x2 grid
  labs(x = "Process", y = "Number Identified") +  # Removed the title
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +  # Use thousand separators on the y-axis
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) + my_theme

p1
```

```{r}
             "interaction"),
  type = c("BP", "BP", "BP", "BP", "BP", "BP", "BP", 
           "CC", "CC", "CC", "CC", "CC", "CC", "CC",

)

# Filter the data to only include rows for "control + heat" treatment

  filter(treatment == "control + heat")

# Ensure the type column is ordered according to the specified order
data_filtered$type <- factor(data_filtered$type, levels = c("BP", "CC", "MF"))

data_filtered$factor <- factor(data_filtered$factor, levels = c("ploidy", "heat", "interaction"))

# Reshape the filtered data to a long format for easier plotting with ggplot2
data_long <- data_filtered %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c("hyper", "hypo"), names_to = "Category", values_to = "Value")

# Generate the bar plot for "control + heat" treatment only

  scale_fill_manual(values = c("ploidy" = "royalblue1", "heat" = "orangered1", "interaction" = "seagreen3")) +  # Custom colors
  facet_wrap(~ type, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +  # Set ncol = 2 for a 2x2 grid
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "Category", y = "DML in enriched genes") +  # Removed the title
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +  # Increase only the upper y-axis limit
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) + my_theme

# Display the plot
p1
```

```{r}
# Load packages
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Data with counts
dml_data <- data.frame(
  DML_Type = c(rep("Ploidy-DML", 2), 
               rep("Desiccation-DML", 2), 
               rep("Interaction-DML", 3)),
  Methylation_Change = c("Hypermethylated", "Hypomethylated",
                         "Hypermethylated", "Hypomethylated",
                         "Hypermethylated", "Hypomethylated", "Contrasting"),
  Count = c(442, 596, 1150, 1201, 28, 49, 123)
)

# Calculate percent within each DML_Type
dml_data <- dml_data %>%
  group_by(DML_Type) %>%
  mutate(Percent = Count / sum(Count) * 100,
         Label = paste0(Count, "\n", round(Percent), "%"))

# Plot
ggplot(dml_data, aes(x = DML_Type, y = Methylation_Change)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, fill = Methylation_Change), shape = 21, color = "black", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Label), size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Hypermethylated" = "red", 
                               "Hypomethylated" = "blue", 
                               "Contrasting" = "gray40")) +
  scale_size(range = c(10, 30), guide = FALSE) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Methylation Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )


# title = "Differentially Methylated Loci by Type and Methylation Direction",

```


```{r}
# Packages
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(gt)

# --- Your data (unchanged) ---
dml <- tibble::tribble(
  ~DML,          ~geneID,     ~Gene_Name,                                           ~Chromosome,     ~start,    ~end,     ~Methylation_Difference, ~Category,
  "ploidy-DML", 105318079, "MAP kinase-activating death domain protein",           "NC_047559.1", 17423557, 17423559,  +22, "Stress response",
  "ploidy-DML", 105328103, "neurexin-1",                                           "NC_047561.1", 51312262, 51312264,  -23, "Calcium binding",
  "ploidy-DML", 105328103, "neurexin-1",                                           "NC_047561.1", 51346481, 51346483,  -32, "Calcium binding",
  "ploidy-DML", 105329309, "nesprin-1",                                            "NC_047561.1", 28607016, 28607018,  +23, "DNA damage response",
  "ploidy-DML", 105329309, "nesprin-1",                                            "NC_047561.1", 28607026, 28607028,  +21, "DNA damage response",
  "ploidy-DML", 105329309, "nesprin-1",                                            "NC_047561.1", 28607119, 28607121,  -24, "DNA damage response",
  "ploidy-DML", 105329309, "nesprin-1",                                            "NC_047561.1", 28608523, 28608525,  +26, "DNA damage response",
  "ploidy-DML", 105329645, "ubiquitin-like-specific protease 1",                   "NC_047561.1", 27733219, 27733221,  -21, "Stress response",
  "ploidy-DML", 105335651, "1-phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate phosphodiesterase beta-1",
                                                                                   "NC_047561.1", 19405662, 19405664,  +22, "Lipid metabolism",
  "ploidy-DML", 105347767, "F-box DNA helicase 1",                                 "NC_047561.1",  2676336,  2676338,  -21, "DNA replication",
  "heat-DML",   105320544, "kinesin-like protein unc-104",                         "NC_047564.1", 40471809, 40471811,  +42, "Cell adhesion, transport",
  "heat-DML",   105326303, "phosphatidylinositol-binding clathrin assembly protein LAP",
                                                                                   "NC_047563.1",  1749458,  1749460,  -20, "Cell proliferation",
  "heat-DML",   105326303, "phosphatidylinositol-binding clathrin assembly protein LAP",
                                                                                   "NC_047563.1",  1761560,  1761562,  +20, "Cell proliferation",
  "heat-DML",   105326303, "phosphatidylinositol-binding clathrin assembly protein LAP",
                                                                                   "NC_047563.1",  1771931,  1771933,  -23, "Cell proliferation",
  "heat-DML",   105326303, "phosphatidylinositol-binding clathrin assembly protein LAP",
                                                                                   "NC_047563.1",  1780314,  1780316,  -28, "Cell proliferation",
  "heat-DML",   105344721, "ataxin-2-like protein",                                "NC_047564.1", 22005779, 22005781,  -21, "Stress response",
  "heat-DML",   117680672, "uncharacterized LOC117680672",                         "NC_047563.1",   684534,   684536,  -21, "Unknown",
  "interaction-DML", 105319299, "CAD protein",                                     "NC_047564.1",  8425110,  8425112,  -31, "Apoptosis",
  "interaction-DML", 105329309, "nesprin-1",                                       "NC_047561.1", 28607016, 28607018,  +21, "DNA damage response",
  "interaction-DML", 105340590, "dihydropyrimidinase",                             "NW_022994979.1", 42498,    42500,  +31, "Stress response"
)

# --- Summarize by CATEGORY (across DML types) ---
# counts and within-DML percentages
cat_summ <- dml %>%
  mutate(DML = factor(DML, levels = c("ploidy-DML","heat-DML","interaction-DML"))) %>%
  count(DML, Category, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(DML) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

# order categories by total count across all DML types (for cleaner y-axis)
cat_order <- cat_summ %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups="drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  pull(Category)

cat_summ <- cat_summ %>%
  mutate(Category = factor(Category, levels = cat_order))

# --- Colors (Okabe–Ito inspired, color-blind friendly) ---
dml_cols <- c("ploidy-DML"="#0072B2", "heat-DML"="#D55E00", "interaction-DML"="#009E73")

# --- Plot: categories by DML type ---
p_cat <- ggplot(cat_summ, aes(x = n, y = Category, fill = DML)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.72, color = "white", alpha = 0.95) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = dml_cols, name = "DML type") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Representation of DML by Functional Category",
    subtitle = "Counts per category, grouped by DML type",
    x = "Number of DML",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 16, 10, 16)
  )

p_cat
# ggsave("dml_by_category.png", p_cat, width = 8.2, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# --- Professional table (gt) with counts and within-DML % ---
tbl <- cat_summ %>%
  mutate(`Count (n)` = n,
         `Percent within DML` = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)) %>%
  select(Category, DML, `Count (n)`, `Percent within DML`) %>%
  arrange(match(Category, cat_order), DML) %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "Category", groupname_col = "DML") %>%
  tab_header(
    title = md("**DML by Functional Category**"),
    subtitle = "Count and % within each DML type"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), data_row.padding = px(6)) %>%
  opt_table_outline() %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#F7F7F7"),
            locations = cells_body(rows = seq(1, n(), by = 2))) %>%
  cols_align(columns = c(`Count (n)`, `Percent within DML`), align = "center") %>%
  tab_source_note(md("Palette: Okabe–Ito; values are within-DML percentages."))

tbl
# gtsave(tbl, "dml_by_category_table.png", expand = 5)  # optional save


```

```{r}
# Load packages
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# ---- Data ----
dml_data <- data.frame(
  DML_Type = c(rep("Ploidy-DML", 2),
               rep("Desiccation-DML", 2),
               rep("Interaction-DML", 3)),
  Methylation_Change = c("Hypermethylated", "Hypomethylated",
                         "Hypermethylated", "Hypomethylated",
                         "Hypermethylated", "Hypomethylated", "Contrasting"),
  Count = c(442, 596, 1150, 1201, 28, 49, 123)
)

# ---- Tidy + nice labels ----
dml_plot <- dml_data %>%
  mutate(
    DML_Type = factor(DML_Type,
                      levels = c("Ploidy-DML", "Desiccation-DML", "Interaction-DML")),
    Methylation_Change = factor(Methylation_Change,
                                levels = c("Hypermethylated", "Hypomethylated", "Contrasting"))
  ) %>%
  group_by(DML_Type) %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = 100 * Count / sum(Count),
    # label on two lines: count and percent (1 decimal)
    Label = paste0(Count, "\n", sprintf("%.1f%%", Percent))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# ---- Colors (color-blind friendly) ----
cols <- c(
  "Hypermethylated" = "#D55E00",   # orange
  "Hypomethylated"  = "#0072B2",   # blue
  "Contrasting"     = "#7A7A7A"    # grey
)

# ---- Plot ----
p <- ggplot(dml_plot, aes(x = DML_Type, y = Methylation_Change)) +
  # bubbles (area scaled by Count)
  geom_point(aes(size = Count, fill = Methylation_Change),
             shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 1.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  # labels centered on bubbles
  geom_text(aes(label = Label), lineheight = 0.95, fontface = "bold", size = 3.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = "Methylation status") +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 28, guide = "none") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title   = "Distribution of DML by Type and Methylation Direction",
    subtitle = "Bubble size = number of DML; label shows count and percent within DML type",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "#555555"),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 16, 12, 16)
  )

p

# ---- Optional: save ----
# ggsave("dml_bubbles.png", p, width = 8, height = 4.8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

```
